title: The Office - Presentation Series 5 - Deferring Questions

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Katherine and as you've noticed on our website, we have a number of lessons about giving a presentation in English.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，正如您在我们的网站上注意到的那样，我们有许多关于用英语进行演示的课程。

segments.en: So this is one of those lessons.
segments.zh: 所以这是这些课程之一。

segments.en: Today we're talking about avoiding questions.
segments.zh: 今天我们谈论的是避免问题。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today in part five of our presentation series, we're going to try and handle some questions or avoid questions as Katherine said.
segments.zh: 今天在我们的演讲系列的第五部分中，我们将尝试处理一些问题或避免问题，正如凯瑟琳所说。

segments.en: So why don't we jump into the dialogue.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不跳进对话。

segments.en: Let's see what Mr. Ford is talking about now and we'll be back in a bit.
segments.zh: 让我们看看福特先生现在在说什么，我们稍后会回来。

segments.en: Now as we've already discussed, there's a huge untapped market out there, both in Asia, in other developing markets and in the more mature markets for us to push into.
segments.zh: 正如刚才所说，无论亚洲、其他发展中市场，还是更成熟的市场，都还有巨大的未开发空间，等着我们进入。

segments.en: Now of course this represents an enormous challenge with enormous rewards for the winners.
segments.zh: 当然，这代表了一个巨大的挑战，对获胜者来说是巨大的回报。

segments.en: But for any new product, we need a great marketing message and marketing campaign.
segments.zh: 但对于任何新产品，我们都需要一个伟大的营销信息和营销活动。

segments.en: It needs to be directed and focused at our target consumer and needs to be pitched at exactly the right level.
segments.zh: 它需要针对我们的目标消费者，并需要在正确的水平上进行宣传。

segments.en: The question we must first address is of course, who is our target consumer and secondly, what do they expect from the next generation alpha laptop?
segments.zh: 我们必须首先解决的问题是，谁是我们的目标消费者，其次，他们对下一代 Alpha 笔记本电脑有什么期望？

segments.en: Let's first of all tackle the first question.
segments.zh: 让我们首先解决第一个问题。

segments.en: Our target consumer for the X420 is the middle class white collar worker with an above average income.
segments.zh: X420的目标消费者是收入高于平均水平的中产阶级白领工人。

segments.en: However, as we mentioned before, the total number of computer owners is expanding rapidly and we need to broaden our audience for this product.
segments.zh: 然而，正如我们之前提到的，计算机所有者的总数正在迅速扩大，我们需要扩大该产品的受众。

segments.en: For example, the X420 is also ideally suited to the younger student sector who might use laptops both for studying and gaming.
segments.zh: 例如，X420 也非常适合年轻学生，他们既可以用笔记本学习，也可以用它玩游戏。

segments.en: There's no doubt that...
segments.zh: 毫无疑问...

segments.en: Mr. Ford, if I could just interrupt a moment.
segments.zh: 福特先生，我能否打断一下。

segments.en: You say that the computer is suitable for students, but you don't think the price of the X420 is just too much for most students?
segments.zh: 你说电脑适合学生，但你不认为X420的价格对大多数学生来说太贵了吗？

segments.en: Well that's a fair point.
segments.zh: 这个问题提得有道理。

segments.en: If you don't mind, I'd like to tackle your question a little bit later in the Q&A section.
segments.zh: 如果您不介意，我想稍后在问答部分中解决您的问题。

segments.en: Is that okay?
segments.zh: 这样可以吗？

segments.en: Yes, sure.
segments.zh: 对，当然。

segments.en: Okay, so as I was saying, we have an exciting campaign planned for the X420.
segments.zh: 好的，正如我所说，我们为 X420 计划了一场激动人心的活动。

segments.en: Firstly we'll have a nationwide television campaign as well as advertising on radio and also in many computer publications.
segments.zh: 首先，我们将在全国范围内开展电视活动以及广播和许多计算机出版物的广告。

segments.en: We also intend to...
segments.zh: 我们也打算...

segments.en: I'm sorry to stop you Mr. Ford, but do you really think that a television campaign is cost effective?
segments.zh: 很抱歉打断您，福特先生，但您真的认为电视宣传具有成本效益吗？

segments.en: I mean, how much does that go into cost?
segments.zh: 我的意思是，这要花多少钱？

segments.en: Well I don't have the figures to hand, but I'd be happy to discuss those figures with you after the presentation.
segments.zh: 好吧，我手头没有这些数字，但我很乐意在演示结束后与您讨论。

segments.en: Okay let me just go on to talk a little more about the exciting campaign we have in store.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我继续谈谈我们即将推出的令人兴奋的活动。

segments.en: All right we're back and now we can get started with Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，现在我们可以开始使用语言要点。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Okay so Marco, a lot of the conversation today was about markets and a target consumer.
segments.zh: 好吧，马可，今天的很多谈话都是关于市场和目标消费者的。

segments.en: So perhaps we should start talking a little bit about who Mr. Ford thinks this company's consumers are.
segments.zh: 所以也许我们应该开始谈谈福特先生认为这家公司的消费者是谁。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: He mentioned that the Alpha laptop could also be aimed at the middle class.
segments.zh: 他提到阿尔法笔记本电脑也可以针对中产阶级。

segments.en: We have different classes in society, especially in America, where we talk about people who are low income, they don't make very much money, or people who make a lot of money, they're rich, they're on top.
segments.zh: 我们在社会上有不同的阶级，尤其是在美国，我们谈论低收入的人，他们没有赚很多钱，或者赚很多钱的人，他们很富有，他们处于社会顶层。

segments.en: That's the high class.
segments.zh: 那是上层阶级。

segments.en: Yeah, high class.
segments.zh: 是的，上层阶级。

segments.en: But in the middle, we have the middle class.
segments.zh: 但在中间，我们有中产阶级。

segments.en: And this is just average people.
segments.zh: 这只是普通人。

segments.en: They make money, they have a car.
segments.zh: 他们赚钱，他们有车。

segments.en: They're not rich, but they're not poor.
segments.zh: 他们并不富有，但他们并不穷。

segments.en: Okay so they're in the middle.
segments.zh: 好的，所以他们在中间。

segments.en: So this is the middle class.
segments.zh: 所以这是中产阶级。

segments.en: The computer is aimed at the middle class market, but he said that it's middle class white collar worker.
segments.zh: 这台电脑是针对中产阶级市场的，但他说它是中产阶级的白领工人。

segments.en: Okay so I know this phrase exists in many other languages, but a white collar worker in English means, refers to the color of the shirt that you wear.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我知道这句话存在于许多其他语言中，但英语中的白领工人是指您穿的衬衫的颜色。

segments.en: So white collar workers usually work in offices.
segments.zh: 所以白领工人通常在办公室工作。

segments.en: So because they're usually wearing suits.
segments.zh: 因为他们通常穿着西装。

segments.en: That's right, they have to wear nice clothes like suits and button down shirts.
segments.zh: 没错，他们必须穿漂亮的衣服，比如西装和纽扣衬衫。

segments.en: But we sometimes also talk about blue collar workers.
segments.zh: 但我们有时也会谈论蓝领工人。

segments.en: Who are these guys?
segments.zh: 这些人是谁？

segments.en: Blue collar workers are usually people that are in trades, like for example a mechanic or a plumber, because usually you see them wearing those blue shirts.
segments.zh: 蓝领工人通常是从事行业的人，例如机械师或水管工，因为您通常会看到他们穿着这些蓝色衬衫。

segments.en: Yeah, uniforms.
segments.zh: 是的，制服。

segments.en: They're usually people who work with their hands or who are not likely to work in a big office.
segments.zh: 他们通常是用手工作或不太可能在大办公室工作的人。

segments.en: So usually maybe these people are not middle class, maybe they are lower class.
segments.zh: 所以通常这些人不是中产阶级，也许他们是下层阶级。

segments.en: They can be both.
segments.zh: 他们可以两者兼而有之。

segments.en: In America right now I think you can make quite a bit of money if you're a plumber or construction worker.
segments.zh: 现在在美国，我认为如果你是一名管道工或建筑工人，你可以赚很多钱。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: But he also mentioned middle class white collar worker with an above average income.
segments.zh: 但他也提到了收入高于平均水平的中产阶级白领工人。

segments.en: Okay so an income is the amount of money that a person earns, usually in a year.
segments.zh: 好吧，收入是一个人通常在一年内赚取的金额。

segments.en: So we say $30,000 a year.
segments.zh: 所以我们说每年 30,000 美元。

segments.en: That's your annual income.
segments.zh: 那是你的年收入。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So when we talk about something that's average, that means it's normal.
segments.zh: 因此，当我们谈论平均水平时，这意味着它是正常的。

segments.en: But in this case we're not talking about something that's average.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，我们不是在谈论平均水平。

segments.en: What are we talking about?
segments.zh: 我们在说什么？

segments.en: It's above average.
segments.zh: 它高于平均水平。

segments.en: Above average.
segments.zh: 高于平均水平。

segments.en: So if the average income of a person in America is $36,000 a year, an above average income is $70,000 a year or $65,000 a year.
segments.zh: 因此，如果一个人在美国的平均收入为每年 36,000 美元，则高于平均收入为每年 70,000 美元或每年 65,000 美元。

segments.en: But for the middle class maybe that's different.
segments.zh: 但对于中产阶级来说，这可能是不同的。

segments.en: So in the middle class an average annual income is $70,000.
segments.zh: 所以在中产阶级的平均年收入是 70,000 美元。

segments.en: An above average income in the middle class is $120,000 a year.
segments.zh: 中产阶级的平均收入为每年 120,000 美元。

segments.en: So the phrase there above average, you're just referring to something that's more than the normal.
segments.zh: 所以 above average 这个短语，指的就是比正常情况更多。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So in this case more than the normal income for a middle class worker.
segments.zh: 因此，在这种情况下，中产阶级工人的收入高于正常收入。

segments.en: You can also say below average.
segments.zh: 你也可以说低于平均水平。

segments.en: So a below average income is lower than most people earn.
segments.zh: 所以低于平均水平的收入低于大多数人的收入。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And well continuing on talking about markets and the demographics, who were selling the computer to, we also talked about our target consumer.
segments.zh: 继续谈市场和人口统计数据，也就是我们在把电脑卖给谁，我们还谈到了目标消费者。

segments.en: This is something that you often hear in meetings at work or in marketing departments.
segments.zh: 这是您在工作或营销部门的会议中经常听到的内容。

segments.en: A target is something you aim for.
segments.zh: 所谓 target，就是你要瞄准的东西。

segments.en: It's something you want to hit or achieve.
segments.zh: 这是您想要达到或实现的目标。

segments.en: And so a target consumer is the buyer, is a customer that you aim to have.
segments.zh: 因此，目标消费者是买方，是您想要拥有的客户。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So maybe you have some customers that they're students and you have some customers that they're very old, but your target consumer are the people that you really want to reach out to.
segments.zh: 所以也许你有一些客户是学生，有一些客户年纪很大，但你的目标消费者是你真正想争取的人。

segments.en: In this case, the middle class white collar worker.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，中产阶级白领工人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So in the case of our dialogue, our target consumer is a middle class white collar worker, for example.
segments.zh: 因此，在我们的对话中，我们的目标消费者是中产阶级白领工人。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a lot of marketing stuff here talking about the computer and what Mr. Ford was saying.
segments.zh: 所以这里有很多营销内容谈论计算机和福特先生所说的话。

segments.en: Let's take a pause.
segments.zh: 让我们暂停一下。

segments.en: Let's listen to the dialogue again and we'll be back with some phrases on how to defer questions.
segments.zh: 让我们再听一次对话，之后我们会回来讲一些关于如何延后回答提问的短语。

segments.en: Now as we've already discussed, there's a huge untapped market out there, both in Asia and other developing markets and in the more mature markets for us to push into.
segments.zh: 现在正如我们已经讨论过的，在亚洲和其他发展中市场以及更成熟的市场中，有一个巨大的尚未开发的市场供我们推进。

segments.en: Now of course this represents an enormous challenge with enormous rewards for the winners.
segments.zh: 当然，这代表了一个巨大的挑战，对获胜者来说是巨大的回报。

segments.en: But for any new product, we need a great marketing message and marketing campaign.
segments.zh: 但对于任何新产品，我们都需要一个伟大的营销信息和营销活动。

segments.en: It needs to be directed and focused at our target consumer and needs to be pitched at exactly the right level.
segments.zh: 它需要针对我们的目标消费者，并需要在正确的水平上进行宣传。

segments.en: The question we must first address is of course, who is our target consumer?
segments.zh: 我们必须首先解决的问题是，我们的目标消费者是谁？

segments.en: And secondly, what do they expect from the next generation alpha laptop?
segments.zh: 其次，他们对下一代 Alpha 笔记本电脑有什么期望？

segments.en: Let's first of all tackle the first question.
segments.zh: 让我们首先解决第一个问题。

segments.en: Our target consumer for the X420 is the middle class white collar worker with an above average income.
segments.zh: X420的目标消费者是收入高于平均水平的中产阶级白领工人。

segments.en: However, as we mentioned before, the total number of computer owners is expanding rapidly and we need to broaden our audience for this product.
segments.zh: 然而，正如我们之前提到的，计算机所有者的总数正在迅速扩大，我们需要扩大该产品的受众。

segments.en: For example, the X420 is also ideally suited to the younger student sector who might use laptops both for studying and gaming.
segments.zh: 例如，X420 也非常适合年轻学生，他们既可以用笔记本学习，也可以用它玩游戏。

segments.en: There's no doubt that...
segments.zh: 毫无疑问...

segments.en: Mr. Ford, if I could just interrupt a moment.
segments.zh: 福特先生，我能否打断一下。

segments.en: You say that the computer is suitable for students, but you don't think the price of the X420 is just too much for most students?
segments.zh: 你说电脑适合学生，但你不认为X420的价格对大多数学生来说太贵了吗？

segments.en: Well that's a fair point.
segments.zh: 嗯，这话说得有道理。

segments.en: If you don't mind, I'd like to tackle your question a little bit later in the Q&A section.
segments.zh: 如果您不介意，我想稍后在问答部分中解决您的问题。

segments.en: Is that okay?
segments.zh: 这样可以吗？

segments.en: Yes, sure.
segments.zh: 对，当然。

segments.en: Okay, so as I was saying, we have an exciting campaign planned for the X420.
segments.zh: 好的，正如我所说，我们为 X420 计划了一场激动人心的活动。

segments.en: Firstly we'll have a nationwide television campaign as well as advertising on radio and also in many computer publications.
segments.zh: 首先，我们将在全国范围内开展电视活动以及广播和许多计算机出版物的广告。

segments.en: We also intend to...
segments.zh: 我们也打算...

segments.en: I'm sorry to stop you Mr. Ford, but do you really think that a television campaign is cost effective?
segments.zh: 很抱歉打断您，福特先生，但您真的认为电视宣传具有成本效益吗？

segments.en: I mean, how much does that go into cost?
segments.zh: 我的意思是，这要花多少钱？

segments.en: Well I don't have the figures to hand, but I'd be happy to discuss those figures with you after the presentation.
segments.zh: 好吧，我手头没有这些数字，但我很乐意在演示结束后与您讨论。

segments.en: Okay, let me just go on to talk a little more about the exciting campaign we have in store.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我继续谈谈我们即将推出的激动人心的活动。

segments.en: Alright we're back, so now let's take a look at those phrases that we mentioned on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，所以现在让我们来看看我们在流利表达上提到的那些短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: So Marco, there was a phrase that I heard twice in today's dialogue that I think we should talk about.
segments.zh: 所以马可，今天的对话里有个短语我听到了两次，我觉得我们应该讲讲。

segments.en: The verb is to tackle, so we heard to tackle a question.
segments.zh: 这个动词是 to tackle，我们听到了 to tackle a question 这个搭配。

segments.en: Right, so when Mr. Ford says, I'll tackle that question a little bit later on, he's talking about I'll answer the question or I'll talk about that question later on.
segments.zh: 对，所以当福特先生说，我稍后会解决这个问题时，他在谈论我会回答这个问题，或者我稍后会谈论这个问题。

segments.en: Right, but in this word to tackle, there's something kind of physical about it because in football we say that when someone tries to hit the ball from someone else, it's a slide tackle.
segments.zh: 对，但 to tackle 这个词有种身体动作的意味，因为在足球里，当有人试图从别人脚下抢球时，那叫滑铲（slide tackle）。

segments.en: And so to tackle a question means to really jump into it and try and solve it and it's you know maybe not an easy question.
segments.zh: 因此，解决一个问题意味着真正跳入并尝试解决它，这您知道可能不是一个简单的问题。

segments.en: So I'm going to tackle that later.
segments.zh: 所以我稍后会解决这个问题。

segments.en: I'm going to tackle a challenge.
segments.zh: 我要应对挑战。

segments.en: It's more than just to solve a problem or to answer a question.
segments.zh: 这不仅仅是解决问题或回答问题。

segments.en: So maybe you can also tackle a project, a difficult project.
segments.zh: 所以也许你也可以处理一个项目，一个困难的项目。

segments.en: That's right, so you know what, I'm going to give us two weeks to tackle this project because it's a very difficult one.
segments.zh: 没错，所以你知道吗，我将给我们两周的时间来解决这个项目，因为这是一个非常困难的项目。

segments.en: Alright, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: And well actually when he was getting some questions from the audience members specifically because he was kind of being interrupted, he was very polite about it and to kind of defer the question he said, you know what, that's a fair point but I'll tackle that question later on.
segments.zh: 实际上，他因为有点被打断而接到观众的一些提问时，对此非常礼貌，为了把问题往后推，他说：你知道吗，这话说得有道理，但我稍后会处理这个问题。

segments.en: Okay, and so this is a really great phrase if you want to flatter someone, make them feel good before you tell them that you're not going to answer their question.
segments.zh: 好的，所以如果你想奉承某人，在你告诉他们你不会回答他们的问题之前让他们感觉良好，这是一个非常棒的短语。

segments.en: Or maybe you disagree with someone so I could say, you know what Marco, chocolate cake is the only cake in the entire world that people should eat.
segments.zh: 或者你不同意某人的观点，所以我可以说，你知道马可，巧克力蛋糕是全世界唯一应该吃的蛋糕。

segments.en: Okay, and I could say something like that's a fair point but in my opinion vanilla cake is better.
segments.zh: 好的，我可以说，这话说得有道理，但在我看来香草蛋糕更好。

segments.en: Alright, so see what Marco did?
segments.zh: 好吧，看看马可做了什么？

segments.en: He made me feel good.
segments.zh: 他让我感觉很好。

segments.en: He said, you know, fair point, that's a good idea but I disagree or but in the case of today's dialogue but we'll talk about that later.
segments.zh: 他说，你知道，公平的观点，这是一个好主意，但我不同意，或者在今天的对话中，但我们稍后会讨论。

segments.en: Right, and actually he did another smart thing in the way that he used his language skills here when he was interrupted again he said, hey, you know what, I'd be happy to answer your questions at a later time or in the Q&A session.
segments.zh: 对，实际上，当他再次被打断时，他在这里使用了他的语言技能，他做了另一件聪明的事情，他说，嘿，你知道吗，我很乐意在以后或问答环节中回答你的问题。

segments.en: Okay, so this phrase, I'd be happy to.
segments.zh: 好吧，这句话，我很乐意。

segments.en: I'd be happy to talk about that at a later time but right now I'm trying to explain something else.
segments.zh: 我很乐意在以后谈论这个，但现在我正试图解释其他事情。

segments.en: Exactly, so these are two really, really key phrases for trying to in a nice way change the topic or change the conversation.
segments.zh: 没错，所以这是两个非常非常关键的短语，可以很好地改变主题或改变对话。

segments.en: So yeah, I guess you can say, yeah, I'd be happy to talk about that later on or I'll tackle that question in a little bit or that's a fair point but we'll talk about it later on.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，我想你可以说，是的，我很乐意稍后谈论这个问题，或者我会稍后解决这个问题，或者这是一个公平的观点，但我们稍后会讨论它。

segments.en: Okay, so a lot of great language there.
segments.zh: 好吧，那里有很多很棒的语言。

segments.en: Why don't we take a last listen to our dialogue and review everything we've just learned.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不最后一次听我们的对话，回顾我们刚刚学到的一切。

segments.en: Now as we've already discussed, there's a huge untapped market out there both in Asia, in other developing markets and in the more mature markets for us to push into.
segments.zh: 现在正如我们已经讨论过的那样，亚洲、其他发展中市场和更成熟的市场中都有一个巨大的尚未开发的市场供我们进入。

segments.en: Now of course this represents an enormous challenge with enormous rewards for the winners but for any new product we need a great marketing message and marketing campaign.
segments.zh: 当然，这代表了一个巨大的挑战，对获胜者来说是一个巨大的回报，但对于任何新产品，我们都需要一个伟大的营销信息和营销活动。

segments.en: It needs to be directed and focused at our target consumer and needs to be pitched at exactly the right level.
segments.zh: 它需要针对我们的目标消费者，并需要在正确的水平上进行宣传。

segments.en: The question we must first address is of course who is our target consumer and secondly what do they expect from the next generation alpha laptop?
segments.zh: 我们必须首先解决的问题当然是我们的目标消费者是谁，其次他们对下一代 Alpha 笔记本电脑有什么期望？

segments.en: Let's first of all tackle the first question.
segments.zh: 让我们首先解决第一个问题。

segments.en: Our target consumer for the X420 is the middle class white collar worker with an above average income.
segments.zh: X420的目标消费者是收入高于平均水平的中产阶级白领工人。

segments.en: However, as we mentioned before, the total number of computer owners is expanding rapidly and we need to broaden our audience for this product.
segments.zh: 然而，正如我们之前提到的，计算机所有者的总数正在迅速扩大，我们需要扩大该产品的受众。

segments.en: For example, the X420 is also ideally suited to the younger student sector who might use laptops both for studying and gaming.
segments.zh: 例如，X420 也非常适合年轻学生，他们既可以用笔记本学习，也可以用它玩游戏。

segments.en: There is no doubt that…
segments.zh: 毫无疑问……

segments.en: Mr. Ford, if I could just interrupt a moment.
segments.zh: 福特先生，我能否打断一下。

segments.en: You say that the computer is suitable for students but you don't think the price of the X420 is just too much for most students?
segments.zh: 你说电脑适合学生，但你不认为X420的价格对大多数学生来说太贵了吗？

segments.en: Well that's a fair point.
segments.zh: 嗯，这话说得有道理。

segments.en: If you don't mind, I'd like to tackle your question a little bit later in the Q&A section.
segments.zh: 如果您不介意，我想稍后在问答部分中解决您的问题。

segments.en: Is that okay?
segments.zh: 这样可以吗？

segments.en: Yes, sure.
segments.zh: 对，当然。

segments.en: Okay, so as I was saying, we have an exciting campaign planned for the X420.
segments.zh: 好的，正如我所说，我们为 X420 计划了一场激动人心的活动。

segments.en: Firstly we'll have a nationwide television campaign as well as advertising on radio and also in many computer publications.
segments.zh: 首先，我们将在全国范围内开展电视活动以及广播和许多计算机出版物的广告。

segments.en: We also intend to…
segments.zh: 我们还打算…

segments.en: I'm sorry to stop you Mr. Ford, but do you really think that a television campaign is cost effective?
segments.zh: 很抱歉打断您，福特先生，但您真的认为电视宣传具有成本效益吗？

segments.en: I mean, how much does that go into cost?
segments.zh: 我的意思是，这要花多少钱？

segments.en: Well I don't have the figures to hand, but I'd be happy to discuss those figures with you after the presentation.
segments.zh: 好吧，我手头没有这些数字，但我很乐意在演示结束后与您讨论。

segments.en: Okay let me just go on to talk a little more about the exciting campaign we have in store.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我继续谈谈我们即将推出的令人兴奋的活动。

segments.en: All right, so this was part five of our presentation series.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是我们演示系列的第五部分。

segments.en: We're halfway done with it and so far we've seen a lot of interesting things and as you notice it's an intermediate lesson so it is a little bit more challenging and a little bit longer than your previous lessons.
segments.zh: 我们已经完成了一半，到目前为止我们看到了很多有趣的内容，你会发现这是一节中级课程，所以比你之前的课程更具挑战性，也更长一点。

segments.en: That's right, these are longer and some of the phrases that you've learned, these words are very difficult.
segments.zh: 没错，这些更长，你学到的一些短语，这些词非常困难。

segments.en: But as a reminder, some of the words repeat.
segments.zh: 但作为提醒，有些词重复了。

segments.en: So for example in today's dialogue we heard a lot about developing markets and campaigns, but we also heard about these last week in episode four.
segments.zh: 因此，例如在今天的对话中，我们听到了很多关于发展中市场和活动的信息，但我们在上周的第四集中也听说了这些。

segments.en: So if you're confused or you want some extra practice, I would recommend listening to some of the older lessons again just to review because you're going to hear a lot of these words and phrases over and over again.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您感到困惑或想要一些额外的练习，我建议您再次听一些较早的课程来复习，因为您会一遍又一遍地听到很多这些单词和短语。

segments.en: That's right and of course if you have any questions about this or any suggestions you can also come to our website EnglishPod.com where we'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 没错，当然，如果您对此有任何疑问或任何建议，您也可以访问我们的网站 englishpod.com，我们将在那里见到每个人。

segments.en: That's right, so until next week, bye everyone.
segments.zh: 没错，所以直到下周，再见大家。
